_comment: Curated ground-truth pairs for the Nautical evaluation harness. Every entry is verifiable from docs/some_lyrics.txt (English, in-scope). This file is hand-maintained, not scraped: web lyric pages returned unreliable/garbled text, so auto-seeding would corrupt the harness. Add hand-verified pairs and re-run `nautical eval`.
_excluded: Out of scope for Step One and intentionally omitted: English-Japanese cross-language echoes, and word-transformation puns (pun-stoppable, Ina-terested, Ina-sanity) that rely on reshaping a word rather than matching existing sounds.
_fields: query = search input; expected = the word/phrase we hope to rediscover; mode = single|multiword; anchor = full|tail|0..1; theme (optional) = comma terms for semantic rerank; note (optional) = rationale.

pairs.note: Headline boundary-crossing oronym (TAKOVER: 'we're not a cult / Nonsensical and nautical'). Full-span because the whole phrase is the echo.
Same oronym with a nautical theme; nautical should rank higher than without the theme.
ALKATRAZ: 'keep the record clean and stainless' ... 'acting brainless'. Tail-anchored: the -ainless rhyme is the payload.
Perfect single-word end-rhyme (phonetic control; painless is not in the lyric but shares the -einless tail).
TAKOVER Verse 3: 'have you invested' ... 'all I've requested'.
TAKOVER Verse 3: 'bank on your emotion' ... 'unwavering devotion'.
Honest hard case (documented Phase 4/6 gap): the reverse decode adds an extra /t/, so 'not a cult' sits far down the pure-phonetic pool. Measured, not asserted to rank top.
Honest hard case: a full-span multi-word echo whose meaning (not just sound) carries it in the song; probes the semantic gap.
